title: Structural induction on Nat
summary: Prove a recursive natural-number identity by splitting into zero and successor cases.
code: theorem add_zero_right (n : Nat) : n + 0 = n := by
triggers: prove a property for all natural numbers using an inductive hypothesis
reason over recursive definitions on Nat or List
prompts: Prove n + 0 = n by induction on n rather than relying on a library lemma.
Split a Nat goal into base case zero and inductive step succ k ih.
invariant: Each constructor of an inductive type produces a subgoal with inductive hypotheses for recursive fields.
mantra: Match the inductive constructors: base case first, then rewrite with ih.
pitfalls: Using cases instead of induction omits the inductive hypothesis ih.

anchors.name: Structured induction
anchors.trick: Use | zero => ... and | succ k ih => ... to keep subgoals explicit.

mutations.explanation: cases does not provide the inductive hypothesis ih needed in the succ branch.
